subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
Given the limited budget, I'm planning a compact but detailed vehicle: an armored interceptor truck with a roof-mounted water cannon turret, neon light bars, corporate decals, and treaded wheels. Since this is a prop rather than a creature, I can likely skip rigging joints and build it as a plain static object, though I still need to think through how the wheels are modeled.

Deciding to give the chassis a root joint with wheel joints, a turret joint, and a cannon joint, keeping the rig simple with six wheels (three per side) for the armored truck proportions. I'm settling on dimensions around 5.2m long, 2.3m wide, and 2.2m tall, oriented facing +Z, using box and cylinder geometries with careful axis orientation for the wheel axles, and setting up a helper function to streamline creating boxes with position and optional bone attachment.

For the body, I'm layering the lower hull as a box with wheels sized to touch the ground, then shaping the cab as another box with a slanted windshield, considering using an extruded profile for the cabin's side silhouette to get that sloped armored look.

Refining the body outline width to 2.2 with paint color, bevel, and smoothing settings, then starting to work out the windshield as a slanted glass plane fitting along the hood's slope points.

I'll angle the windshield plane along the computed normal, giving it a dark glass color with a subtle cyan-magenta HUD-style glow texture. Then I'll add small dark side windows as thin planes positioned on the cab sides near the top.

Now I'm blocking out the hood as a box in front of the cab, sized to fit within the overall 5.6-length hull, then adding a front ram bumper with yellow-black hazard stripe texturing and a trapezoid-extruded push plate.

For the lighting, I'm placing glowing cyan-white headlight boxes on the hood front, a magenta neon bar across the grille, dark vent slats between them, plus a roof-mounted light bar with alternating red/blue glow segments and cyan neon strips running along the hull sides.

Now I'm working on a side decal: an invented corporate logo "ORBITEK PEACEKEEPING" rendered as an SVG texture with hexagon emblem and stripes, mapped onto a plane oriented along the side of the hull, working through the geometry math to get the text facing and orientation correct when viewed from the side.

I'm also designing a roof-mounted water cannon turret with a rotating base ring, housing, and a barrel aimed forward with a flared nozzle, giving it a glowing cyan water effect.

Placing the water tank on the rear roof as a horizontal cylinder with a glowing cyan level window, plus strap rings and end caps, sized to fit the roof's flat section. Positioning the cannon turret and pivot near the tank, working out the geometry for the cannon bar.

Checking wheel positions and width against hull half-width to ensure they protrude correctly without clipping, then adding fender flare boxes above each wheel.

For the wheels themselves I'm building dark rubber cylinders with tread blocks arranged in a ring around the circumference, planning rotation on the X-axis joint and calculating angular positions for each tread block across all six wheels.

Adding lug nut cylinders and a glowing magenta neon torus ring on the wheel's outer face, confirming parts attach correctly in model space under the wheel bone. Still planning additional details like doors with handles, gun-port slits, armor ribs, mirrors, roof antenna, and a rear light bar.

For the aim of around 100-150 parts total, I'm sketching texture needs: an "ORBITEK" hexagon logo texture with cyan/magenta branding, a windshield HUD overlay, and a rear warning texture reading "STAND CLEAR — HYDRANT ACTIVE."

I'm also planning the gauge from the kit, a unit number "RC-07" stenciled on doors/roof/hood, and a grille texture using dark geometric slats with neon edge accents. For the body paint, I'm building a tinted panel material that shades from dark navy near the top to near-black at the underside, with a subtle magenta glow bleeding in near the bottom.

Writing panel paint code...

I'll skip putting a number on the hood or roof since orientation gets tricky for a viewer, and just put numbers on the doors instead. For textured color drawings I'll use white as the tint base, and I'll add a neon glow helper that wraps boxes with a configurable strength, keeping colors as simple strings rather than paint objects.

Now I'm limiting the palette to around 20 flat colors to keep things manageable, and sketching the turret assembly: a base ring at the pivot, a drum-shaped gunmetal turret body, side yoke plates, and the start of the cannon breech box.

Continuing with the barrel geometry—adding reinforcement bands, a flared nozzle cone with a glowing cyan rim and dark inner disc—then working out how to route hoses from the tank to the breech across the turret joint without them stretching unnaturally when the turret rotates.

I'm also planning a gauge panel on the yoke's side plates and a small targeting camera on top of the cannon with a glowing red lens, and figuring out the pitch pose so the barrel tilts slightly without fighting the joint's bone direction.

Now I'm working through the joint hierarchy -- chassis root, then wheel joints, turret, and cannon parented in sequence -- plus adding mirror housings with glowing turn strips and thin seam boxes along the door edges for detail.

Placing the cab door seams, handle, and dark window plane, then positioning the rear logo decal on the side panel with sized dimensions and offset from the hull surface.

Now I'm adding armor skirt details with vented slits, then laying out the neon accent strips—cyan running along the sides and a magenta under-glow box tucked beneath the hull between the wheels for a subtle lighting effect.

For the rear, I'm placing a warning panel plane, red glowing tail light bars, a vertical neon strip, bumper, exhaust vents, and a hitch, making sure the plane orientation and right/up axes work out correctly for a viewer standing behind the vehicle. I'll skip the rear step platform and handrails but keep a simple bumper box, then move to building the front roof light bar with a segmented base spanning across the top.

Adding roof details next: alternating red/blue glow segments, thin rear antennas with glowing tips, a small sensor dome, roof rails, and corner spotlight cylinders on the cab roof. For the front, I'm sketching a bull bar frame with vertical posts and horizontal bars in front of the grille, plus a bumper with hazard stripes and three cylindrical bars running from bumper to hood, keeping the headlight placement in mind.

Working out headlight and grille geometry...

Importing the kit helpers from the clockwork path, then setting up the panelled body with a riveted metal paint texture blending dark blue-grey tones with noise for variation.

Now I'm defining the yellow hazard stripes against a dark base for the chassis markings, flat dark paint for the tires, and steel metal paint for the rims. Writing the tread block loop...
